1	// This file is the business regression guard for scope-name isolation in
2	// organization-level access decisions. Only an actual slash ('/', one byte
3	// 0x2F) is a hierarchy separator: every other byte in a scope segment —
4	// Chinese text, spaces, percent-encoded-looking text, even bytes that are
5	// not valid UTF-8 — is ordinary segment name content. Two requests that
6	// agree in organization, enabled subject, action and resource id and differ
7	// ONLY in the resource scope must therefore be decided by their scope's
8	// original bytes. No case folding, trimming, UTF-8 replacement, percent
9	// decoding or string-prefix reading may move an allow or a deny from one
10	// scope name onto a look-alike.
11	//
12	// The guarded rules, all already implemented by scopeMatches, validateScope
13	// and evaluate in org.go:
14	//
15	//   - An exact (non-recursive) policy matches its scope byte for byte and
16	//     nothing else. After one read allow is published, the same-named scope
17	//     is allowed by it alone; a differently cased name, a name with an extra
18	//     space, and a name that only LOOKS identical because a lone 0xFF, a lone
19	//     0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD display alike cannot borrow the allow. With
20	//     no other matching allow the answer is the default denial
21	//     "no matching allow policy", the hit list is empty, and the version is
22	//     still the published version that was evaluated.
23	//   - When each look-alike name carries its own policy, a request hits only
24	//     the policy bearing its own name; another name's deny never enters its
25	//     hit list or verdict. The single byte 0xFF, the single byte 0xFE and a
26	//     real U+FFFD rune stay three distinct scope names.
27	//   - A recursive policy keeps the exact same name comparison and additionally
28	//     covers true descendants: scopes equal to its raw name, or equal to its
29	//     raw name plus a slash plus more segments. A recursive allow on "org/a"
30	//     reaches "org/a/账本" but never "org/ab/账本"; the literal segment text
31	//     "%2F" is not a slash, so "org/a%2F账本" is a sibling, not a descendant.
32	//     Parents whose own name contains spaces or invalid UTF-8 bytes cover only
33	//     descendants formed by appending a slash to that parent's RAW name.
34	//   - Recursive denies obey the identical boundary: a deny that really matches
35	//     still overrides an allow ("matched deny policy", both identifiers kept in
36	//     ascending order, at the evaluated version), while a deny that misses the
37	//     requested scope name cannot affect another scope's access.
38	//   - A request scope containing consecutive slashes is rejected before any
39	//     policy is evaluated — never silently tidied and then matched. The
40	//     explanation is an explicit invalid-scope reason, version 0 and an empty
41	//     hit list, even when a published allow would cover the tidied path.
42	//
43	// All requests below are envelope-valid apart from the deliberately invalid
44	// scopes: the three organizations agree and the subject is enabled with its
45	// id, the resource id and the action present, so every outcome is genuinely
46	// produced by scope matching or the scope legality check, not by another
47	// envelope rule. The audit half pins that every explanation — allow, policy
48	// deny and default deny — survives the chain, historical review and offline
49	// review with its reason, hit identifiers and actual version intact.
50	package darksafe
51	
52	import (
53		"bytes"
54		"encoding/json"
55		"reflect"
56		"strings"
57		"testing"
58	)
59	
60	// Shared fixture: one organization, one enabled subject, one resource id and
61	// one action. Requests differ only in the resource scope.
62	const (
63		scopeNameOrg        = "acme"
64		scopeNameSubjectID  = "svc-ledger-reader"
65		scopeNameResourceID = "ledger-2026"
66		scopeNameAction     = "read"
67	)
68	
69	// scopeRequest builds an envelope-valid organization request carrying the
70	// given resource scope. Subject and resource organizations agree with the
71	// decision organization and the subject is enabled.
72	func scopeRequest(scope string) OrgRequest {
73		return OrgRequest{
74			SubjectOrg:  scopeNameOrg,
75			ResourceOrg: scopeNameOrg,
76			Subject:     Subject{ID: scopeNameSubjectID, Kind: "service"}, // enabled
77			Resource:    Resource{ID: scopeNameResourceID, Scope: scope},
78			Action:      scopeNameAction,
79		}
80	}
81	
82	// scopePolicy builds one policy for the shared subject, action and scope.
83	func scopePolicy(id, scope string, effect Effect, recursive bool) Policy {
84		return Policy{ID: id, Subject: scopeNameSubjectID, Action: scopeNameAction,
85			Scope: scope, Effect: effect, Recursive: recursive}
86	}
87	
88	// wantScopeDecision pins the full four-field explanation: verdict, reason,
89	// exact hit list (order significant; nil and empty both mean "no hits") and
90	// the version actually evaluated.
91	func wantScopeDecision(t *testing.T, got Decision, allowed bool, reason string, matched []string, version int, context string) {
92		t.Helper()
93		if got.Allowed != allowed {
94			t.Fatalf("%s: allowed = %v, want %v; decision = %+v", context, got.Allowed, allowed, got)
95		}
96		if got.Reason != reason {
97			t.Fatalf("%s: reason = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, got.Reason, reason, got)
98		}
99		if got.Version != version {
100			t.Fatalf("%s: version = %d, want %d; decision = %+v", context, got.Version, version, got)
101		}
102		gotMatched := got.Matched
103		if len(gotMatched) == 0 {
104			gotMatched = nil
105		}
106		wantMatched := matched
107		if len(wantMatched) == 0 {
108			wantMatched = nil
109		}
110		if !reflect.DeepEqual(gotMatched, wantMatched) {
111			t.Fatalf("%s: matched = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, gotMatched, wantMatched, got)
112		}
113	}
114	
115	// TestExactScopeNameGrantsOnlyTheIdenticalScope is the core isolation guard:
116	// one exact read allow published on one scope name admits the same-named
117	// request and no look-alike. Each look-alike is a legal scope (so it reaches
118	// policy evaluation at the published version) but matches nothing, hence the
119	// default denial with an empty hit list at version 1 rather than the allow.
120	func TestExactScopeNameGrantsOnlyTheIdenticalScope(t *testing.T) {
121		exact := "org/账本" // Chinese segment name, valid UTF-8
122		s := NewStore()
123		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
124			scopePolicy("p-exact-allow", exact, EffectAllow, false),
125		})
126		if err != nil || version != 1 {
127			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
128		}
129	
130		// The same-named request hits its own allow and is admitted by it alone.
131		same := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(exact))
132		wantScopeDecision(t, same, true, "matched allow policy",
133			[]string{"p-exact-allow"}, 1, "byte-identical scope")
134	
135		// Every look-alike is a DIFFERENT scope name: it may not borrow the
136		// allow, hits nothing, and falls through to the default denial at the
137		// version actually evaluated. None is an invalid request shape.
138		lookAlikes := map[string]string{
139			"different case in ascii segment": "Org/账本",
140			"extra leading space":             " org/账本",
141			"extra trailing space":            "org/账本 ",
142			"extra space inside the name":     "org/账 本",
143			"extra slash-separated space seg": "org/ /账本",
144		}
145		for name, scope := range lookAlikes {
146			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
147			wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",
148				nil, 1, name+" must not match "+showScope(exact))
149		}
150	
151		// The allow really was available: re-deciding the exact scope after the
152		// look-alikes still admits, proving the denials came from name mismatch.
153		again := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(exact))
154		wantScopeDecision(t, again, true, "matched allow policy",
155			[]string{"p-exact-allow"}, 1, "exact scope after look-alike probes")
156	}
157	
158	// rawByteScopes returns the three byte-different-but-display-conflated scope
159	// names used by this file. The path shape is identical and exactly one
160	// segment byte differs: a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE, and a genuine U+FFFD code
161	// point (valid UTF-8, the three bytes EF BF BD).
162	func rawByteScopes() (withFF, withFE, withReplacement string) {
163		return "org/账" + invalidByte + "本",
164			"org/账" + anotherInvalidByte + "本",
165			"org/账" + replacementRune + "本"
166	}
167	
168	// TestRawByteScopeNamesStayDistinct guards the display-confusable triple in
169	// the scope path: JSON renders the lone 0xFF and lone 0xFE identically, but
170	// authorization compares raw bytes. With one exact allow on the 0xFF name,
171	// neither the 0xFE name nor the genuine-U+FFFD name (nor the 0xFF name with
172	// an extra space) may be admitted; each gets the default denial at the
173	// evaluated version.
174	func TestRawByteScopeNamesStayDistinct(t *testing.T) {
175		scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD := rawByteScopes()
176	
177		// Document the premise: Go distinguishes all three, while encoding/json
178		// collapses the two lone invalid bytes to one rendering. Any matching
179		// layer that normalized before comparing would fail this regression.
180		if scopeFF == scopeFE || scopeFF == scopeFD || scopeFE == scopeFD {
181			t.Fatalf("test premise broken: scopes must differ pairwise: %q %q %q", scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD)
182		}
183		jFF, _ := json.Marshal(scopeFF)
184		jFE, _ := json.Marshal(scopeFE)
185		if !bytes.Equal(jFF, jFE) {
186			t.Fatalf("test premise broken: JSON renders the invalid bytes differently: %s vs %s", jFF, jFE)
187		}
188	
189		s := NewStore()
190		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
191			scopePolicy("p-scope-ff-allow", scopeFF, EffectAllow, false),
192		})
193		if err != nil || version != 1 {
194			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
195		}
196	
197		allowFF := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFF))
198		wantScopeDecision(t, allowFF, true, "matched allow policy",
199			[]string{"p-scope-ff-allow"}, 1, "0xFF scope hits its own allow")
200	
201		// The look-alikes are legal scopes that match nothing: default denial,
202		// empty hit list, but still evaluated at published version 1 — never an
203		// envelope rejection and never the 0xFF allow.
204		lookAlikes := map[string]string{
205			"lone 0xFE look-alike":          scopeFE,
206			"genuine U+FFFD look-alike":     scopeFD,
207			"0xFF name with a trailing sp.": scopeFF + " ",
208			"0xFF name with a leading sp.":  " " + scopeFF,
209		}
210		for name, scope := range lookAlikes {
211			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
212			wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",

3	// their material differently — one reads an organization's live history
4	// and version snapshots, the other a chain-validated export paired with its
5	// separately retained checkpoint — but once the recorded request and the
6	// version it actually used are in hand, both replay the exact same
7	// judgment. That judgment lives only here so the two entry points can never
8	// drift on version-zero handling, envelope rejection order, or how a
9	// historical policy set is evaluated.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	// replayStatus reports whether replayRecordedDecision produced a decision
13	// or why the declared version could not be replayed.
14	type replayStatus int
15	
16	const (
17		// replayDecided means a Decision was recomputed.
18		replayDecided replayStatus = iota
19		// replayVersionAbsent means content for the declared version exists
20		// nowhere in the reviewer's material.
21		replayVersionAbsent
22		// replayVersionAfterTarget means the version's content exists, but only
23		// in a policy change record positioned after the reviewed decision.
24		// Online material never yields this: live version snapshots carry no
25		// position relative to audit records.
26		replayVersionAfterTarget
27	)
28	
29	// versionPolicies is one resolver verdict: either the detached full policy
30	// set of the requested version, or a status explaining why it is unusable.
31	type versionPolicies struct {
32		policies []Policy
33		status   replayStatus
34	}
35	
36	// resolveVersionPolicies supplies the full content of a non-zero version
37	// named by a reviewed decision. Implementations are responsible for
38	// detaching the returned policies from any state or input material.
39	type resolveVersionPolicies func(version int) versionPolicies
40	
41	// replayRecordedDecision re-judges a recorded request against the version
42	// the record declares it actually used. Later publishes or rollbacks are
43	// never substituted for that version.
44	//
45	// A version-0 record first replays the envelope rejections in their fixed
46	// order (missing organizations and identifiers, empty action, organization
47	// mismatch, illegal scope, disabled subject); a request that passes is the
48	// "organization has no published version" denial.
49	//
50	// For a non-zero record the version is resolved before any request rule is
51	// applied: a missing, or only-later, version is an error the caller turns
52	// into ErrVersionNotFound and must never be masked by an envelope denial,
53	// even for a disabled subject. Once the version is in hand, the same
54	// envelope checks run before policy evaluation, so a rejection reports
55	// version 0 with no matched policies regardless of what the version
56	// contains. Evaluation itself is the historical policy set only: deny
57	// overrides allow, matched identifiers are sorted, resource restrictions
58	// narrow rather than replace scope matching, and subject roles never stand
59	// in for an organization policy.
60	func replayRecordedDecision(org string, req OrgRequest, version int, resolve resolveVersionPolicies) (Decision, replayStatus) {
61		if version == 0 {
62			// The original evaluation used no published version: replay the
63			// envelope rejections exactly, in their recorded order, then the
64			// not-yet-published denial.
65			if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
66				return d, replayDecided
67			}
68			return Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: "organization has no published version"}, replayDecided
69		}
70		// Resolve the version first. A request the envelope would reject must
71		// not turn a missing or later-only declared version into an ordinary
72		// denial.
73		resolved := resolve(version)
74		if resolved.status != replayDecided {
75			return Decision{}, resolved.status
76		}
77		// The version exists as claimed, but chain integrity does not imply the
78		// request was admissible: re-run the same envelope checks the online
79		// decision runs before any policy is consulted. A rejection here
80		// evaluates no policies, hence version 0 and no matches, even when the
81		// version holds a fully matching allow policy.
82		if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
83			return d, replayDecided
84		}
85		return evaluate(req, resolved.policies, version), replayDecided
86	}

1	// Command org_decision_example shows why one subject gets different answers
2	// from the role-based demo core (Access) and the organization-level policy
3	// engine (Store.Decide): the two are separate authorization bases. Access
4	// trusts the subject's roles; Decide ignores roles entirely and evaluates
5	// only the decision organization's published policies.
6	//
7	// Run with:
8	//
9	//	go run ./examples/org_decision
10	//
11	// The program takes no arguments, writes no files, and works fully offline.
12	// One subject carrying the owner role reads one ledger:
13	//
14	//  1. Access allows it, because the owner role is enough for the demo core.
15	//  2. A fresh Store denies the same read, because the organization has not
16	//     published any policy yet (version 0: no published policy was used).
17	//  3. After publishing one matching allow policy, the identical request is
18	//     allowed and reports the policy it matched and the version it used.
19	//  4. Two envelope boundaries deny before any policy is consulted: a
20	//     disabled subject, and a subject/resource organization that differs
21	//     from the decision organization. Both report version 0 and no matches.
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25		"fmt"
26		"os"
27	
28		"github.com/asdhoaiqqq/darksafe-access/darksafe"
29	)
30	
31	func main() {
32		if err := run(); err != nil {
33			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "org decision example: failed:", err)
34			os.Exit(1)
35		}
36	}
37	
38	func run() error {
39		// One organization, one ledger, one subject. The subject carries the
40		// owner role, which is decisive for Access and meaningless for Decide.
41		const org = "acme factory"
42		const (
43			ledgerID    = "ledger-2026"
44			ledgerScope = "acme/factory/ledger"
45			subjectID   = "svc-audit-reader"
46		)
47		subject := darksafe.Subject{ID: subjectID, Kind: "service", Roles: []string{"owner"}}
48		ledger := darksafe.Resource{ID: ledgerID, Scope: ledgerScope}
49	
50		// 1. The demo entry point's basis: roles. owner grants the read.
51		printDecision("access  (role owner, no policy store)", darksafe.Access(subject, ledger, "read"))
52	
53		// 2. The organization-level basis: published policies. The request
54		// envelope is valid (all three organizations agree, the scope is legal),
55		// but nothing has been published, so the default is denial and the
56		// version is 0 — no published policy was evaluated.
57		store := darksafe.NewStore()
58		req := darksafe.OrgRequest{
59			SubjectOrg:  org,
60			ResourceOrg: org,
61			Subject:     subject,
62			Resource:    ledger,
63			Action:      "read",
64		}
65		printDecision("decide  (no published policy)      ", store.Decide(org, req))
66	
67		// 3. Publish one allow policy matching this subject, the read action and
68		// the ledger scope, then submit the identical request again.
69		version, err := store.Publish(org, 0, []darksafe.Policy{{
70			ID:      "p-ledger-read-2026",
71			Subject: subjectID,
72			Action:  "read",
73			Scope:   ledgerScope,
74			Effect:  darksafe.EffectAllow,
75		}})
76		if err != nil {
77			return fmt.Errorf("publish allow policy: %w", err)
78		}
79		fmt.Printf("published allow policy p-ledger-read-2026 as version %d\n", version)
80		printDecision("decide  (allow policy published)   ", store.Decide(org, req))
81	
82		// Boundary 1: the same subject disabled. The matching allow policy is
83		// still published, but the envelope check rejects first — no policy is
84		// evaluated, so the version is 0 and the matched list is empty.
85		disabled := req
86		disabled.Subject.Disabled = true
87		printDecision("decide  (subject disabled)         ", store.Decide(org, disabled))
88	
89		// Boundary 2: the subject's organization differs from the decision
90		// organization (a resource-organization mismatch denies the same way).
91		// Again no policy is evaluated: version 0, no matches.
92		cross := req
93		cross.SubjectOrg = "other org"
94		printDecision("decide  (subject org mismatch)     ", store.Decide(org, cross))
95		return nil
96	}
97

99	// allowed or not, the reason, the matched list (roles for Access, policy
100	// IDs for Decide) and the policy version actually used (0 when none was).
101	func printDecision(label string, d darksafe.Decision) {
102		fmt.Printf("%s: allowed=%v reason=%q matched=%q version=%d\n",
103			label, d.Allowed, d.Reason, d.Matched, d.Version)
104	}

1	// This file implements offline review of a single audited decision. It
2	// works solely from exported audit material: the complete record export,
3	// the separately retained checkpoint, and a target sequence. No Store is
4	// created or restored, so an organization can confirm why an access was
5	// allowed or denied long after the service instance that decided it has
6	// ended.
7	//
8	// The complete input must first validate as an audit chain. The policy
9	// version a decision actually used is recovered exclusively from policy
10	// change records preceding that decision within the same organization's
11	// export; later publishes or rollbacks, and a wider later export, cannot
12	// change the recomputed result.
13	//
14	// A review that already holds the material as decoded records
15	// (RecheckDecisionOffline) and one that starts from an archive file
16	// (DecodeAuditArchive followed by a review) historically each ran the full
17	// VerifyAudit chain check on their own, so `darksafe review` validated the
18	// same material twice per invocation. The two stages now share one pass:
19	// VerifyAudit runs exactly once per review, its result is carried in an
20	// unexported VerifiedAuditMaterial, and the review replays the target from
21	// that already-verified material without re-checking the chain. The
22	// standalone entry points keep validating their own inputs, so neither
23	// requires the caller to have run another entry point first.
24	package darksafe
25	
26	import "fmt"
27	
28	// OfflineDecisionReview compares the decision stored in an audited record
29	// with a decision recomputed purely from the exported material.
30	type OfflineDecisionReview struct {
31		// Seq is the reviewed decision record's sequence.
32		Seq int
33		// Original is the decision preserved in the audited record.
34		Original Decision
35		// Recomputed is the decision evaluated again offline from the saved
36		// request and the policy version it originally used.
37		Recomputed Decision
38		// Consistent reports whether both decisions agree on every field
39		// (allowance, reason, matched policies and version), treating a nil
40		// matched list and an empty matched list as the same.
41		Consistent bool
42	}
43	
44	// VerifiedAuditMaterial is an export that has passed the complete
45	// VerifyAudit chain check against the checkpoint it carries. It is the
46	// boundary between one validation and the review: an entry point that has
47	// just validated the material hands it to RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline,
48	// and the review replays the target without validating the chain a second
49	// time.
50	//
51	// It is intentionally unexported: it can only be produced by this package's
52	// own validating entry points (verifyAuditMaterial, reached from
53	// RecheckDecisionOffline, DecodeAuditArchive and DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive),
54	// never from a caller's assertion. It carries no memo that survives the
55	// call that produced it, so modified material or a different checkpoint

62	}

67	// failure returns no material, so a later stage can never review records
68	// that did not validate.
69	func verifyAuditMaterial(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
70		if verifyAuditObserver != nil {
71			verifyAuditObserver()
72		}
73		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
74			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, err

2	// carries for every audit-side treatment of decision content: the
3	// fingerprint's raw canonical encoder, the valid-UTF-8 test that chooses
4	// between the JSON and raw fingerprint families, the archive writer and
5	// reader, and the detaching copy that keeps stored records independent of
6	// caller slices. Each of those walks the one table below instead of naming
7	// the fields itself, so the fields and their order mean the same thing
8	// everywhere. Adding or changing a decision field here reaches
9	// fingerprinting, the UTF-8 decision, archiving, unarchiving and cloning at
10	// once; no audit path can keep a stale list of its own.
11	//
12	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
13	// historical decision field order — the two organization names, the subject,
14	// the resource, the action, then the decision itself — and the archive
15	// mirrors it field for field. Authorization itself (org.go) is intentionally

29		decisionFieldString decisionFieldKind = iota

32		decisionFieldStringList

1	// This file is the single definition of which outer fields an AuditRecord
2	// carries for every audit-side treatment of record-envelope content: the
3	// fingerprint's JSON and raw canonical encoders, the valid-UTF-8 test that
4	// chooses between the two fingerprint families, and the archive writer and
5	// reader. Each of those walks the one table below instead of naming the
6	// fields itself, so the fields and their order mean the same thing
7	// everywhere. Adding or changing an outer record field here reaches
8	// fingerprinting, the UTF-8 decision, archiving and unarchiving at once; no
9	// audit path can keep a stale list of its own.
10	//
11	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
12	// historical envelope order — organization, sequence, category, the two
13	// payloads, the previous fingerprint — followed by the record's own
14	// fingerprint, which the archive stores but the fingerprint itself never
15	// covers. The contents of the two payloads stay governed by their own
16	// field tables (policy, policy-change and decision); this table only names
17	// which payload sits where in the envelope.
18	package darksafe
19	
20	import "unicode/utf8"
21	
22	// recordFieldKind says how one outer AuditRecord field participates in
23	// fingerprinting and archiving.
24	type recordFieldKind int
25	
26	const (
27		// recordFieldString is a string field written from its exact bytes by
28		// the raw fingerprint encoder and the archive, and encoded as a JSON
29		// string by the legacy fingerprint family.
30		recordFieldString recordFieldKind = iota
31		// recordFieldInt is a non-negative integer field (the sequence number).
32		// It has no UTF-8 representation, so the valid-UTF-8 scan skips it
33		// while both encoders write it.
34		recordFieldInt
35		// recordFieldChange is the policy-change payload slot. Its nil-versus-
36		// present shape is marked explicitly by the raw encoder and the
37		// archive, and omitted from the JSON envelope when absent; which change
38		// content is protected remains decided by the policy-change field
39		// table.
40		recordFieldChange
41		// recordFieldDecision is the decision payload slot, treated exactly
42		// like the policy-change slot; which decision content is protected
43		// remains decided by the decision field table.
44		recordFieldDecision
45	)
46	
47	// recordFieldSpec locates one outer AuditRecord field. The accessors used
48	// depend on the kind: string fields use getString/setString, the sequence
49	// uses getInt/setInt and the payload slots getChange/setChange and
50	// getDecision/setDecision. A field appears in recordFields exactly once,
51	// and that entry is the only place its struct member is named.
52	type recordFieldSpec struct {
53		kind recordFieldKind
54		// jsonKey is the field's name in the legacy JSON fingerprint envelope
55		// and doubles as the envelope-membership marker: every field up to and
56		// including the previous fingerprint has one, while the record's own
57		// fingerprint has none, because a fingerprint can never be an input to
58		// itself. The archive writes every field, envelope member or not.
59		jsonKey     string
60		getString   func(*AuditRecord) string
61		setString   func(*AuditRecord, string)
62		getInt      func(*AuditRecord) int
63		setInt      func(*AuditRecord, int)
64		getChange   func(*AuditRecord) *PolicyChange
65		setChange   func(*AuditRecord, *PolicyChange)
66		getDecision func(*AuditRecord) *DecisionRecord
67		setDecision func(*AuditRecord, *DecisionRecord)
68	}
69

71	// order, which the archive reproduces exactly and then extends with the
72	// record's own fingerprint: Org, Seq, Kind, Change, Decision,
73	// PrevFingerprint, Fingerprint, exactly as the historical encodings placed
74	// them.

76		{
77			kind:      recordFieldString,
78			jsonKey:   "org",
79			getString: func(r *AuditRecord) string { return r.Org },
80			setString: func(r *AuditRecord, s string) { r.Org = s },
81		},

84			jsonKey: "seq",
85			getInt:  func(r *AuditRecord) int { return r.Seq },
86			setInt:  func(r *AuditRecord, v int) { r.Seq = v },
87		},

90			jsonKey:   "kind",
91			getString: func(r *AuditRecord) string { return r.Kind },
92			setString: func(r *AuditRecord, s string) { r.Kind = s },
93		},
94		{
95			kind:      recordFieldChange,
96			jsonKey:   "change",
97			getChange: func(r *AuditRecord) *PolicyChange { return r.Change },
98			setChange: func(r *AuditRecord, c *PolicyChange) { r.Change = c },
99		},
100		{
101			kind:        recordFieldDecision,
102			jsonKey:     "decision",
103			getDecision: func(r *AuditRecord) *DecisionRecord { return r.Decision },
104			setDecision: func(r *AuditRecord, d *DecisionRecord) { r.Decision = d },
105		},
106		{
107			kind:      recordFieldString,
108			jsonKey:   "prev",
109			getString: func(r *AuditRecord) string { return r.PrevFingerprint },
110			setString: func(r *AuditRecord, s string) { r.PrevFingerprint = s },
111		},

116			kind:      recordFieldString,

118			setString: func(r *AuditRecord, s string) { r.Fingerprint = s },

127	// table, so its idea of which outer content the fingerprint protects can
128	// never diverge from the fields the encoders write; the record's own
129	// fingerprint is not an envelope member and is never inspected. Which
130	// strings inside the payloads are protected remains decided by the
131	// policy-change and decision field tables alone.
132	func recordUsesRawBytes(r *AuditRecord) bool {
133		for i := range recordFields {
134			f := &recordFields[i]
135			if f.jsonKey == "" {
136				continue
137			}
138			switch f.kind {
139			case recordFieldString:
140				if !utf8.ValidString(f.getString(r)) {
141					return true
142				}
143			case recordFieldChange:
144				if c := f.getChange(r); c != nil && changeHasNonUTF8(c) {
145					return true
146				}
147			case recordFieldDecision:
148				if d := f.getDecision(r); d != nil && decisionRecordHasNonUTF8(d) {
149					return true
150				}
151			}
152		}
153		return false
154	}
